note: Gibraltar has no price level of its own (no World Bank or ICP level, no spatial survey); it keeps United Kingdom's, by the owner's ruling of 28 October 2026, in its own pound, pegged to sterling one for one.

sources.title: World Bank, World Development Indicators: PPP conversion factor, households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure (LCU per international $) — United Kingdom's, kept by the owner's ruling of 28 October 2026: a territory with no price-level measure of its own takes the level of the country whose currency and market it shares
Gibraltar Laws, Currency Notes Act 2011 (current version, last update 10 Feb 2011), section 6
sources.said: Conversion between currency notes and sterling. 6. The Commissioner shall issue on demand to any person desiring to receive currency notes in Gibraltar, currency notes to the equivalent value (at the rate of one pound for one pound sterling) of sums in sterling lodged with the Commissioner by such person, and shall pay on demand to any person desiring to receive sterling the equivalent value so calculated of currency notes lodged with him by such person
